register.summary: Scope creep from multiple managed service teams adding portal requirements
register.context: Multiple managed service teams are independently adding portal requirements, risking scope creep. Currently In Progress.
mitigation: Enforce a formal change request process for new requirements
Require product owner gate approval before requirements enter the backlog
Use a phased delivery roadmap with MoSCoW prioritisation
register.why: Scope creep is visible: 151 USP issues created in 30 days and 47 open bugs, 5 of them S1. On 2 Oct, 78 items that missed the 30 Sep sprint end were re-dated to 30 Oct, including the three S1 price and Document API bugs, which are still in To Do. 33 items remain past due.
register.action: Enforce the change-request gate named in the mitigation.

register.summary: Gynger API sandbox access required before financing integration
register.context: Financing integration on the Marketplace requires Gynger API sandbox access, which has not yet been granted.
mitigation: Request Gynger sandbox access as early as possible
Build a mock integration layer to unblock development while access is pending
Swap mock layer for real sandbox once access is granted
register.why: Financing modal was part of the PDP story (MT-1217), which closed on 24 Sep. No Jira evidence that Gynger sandbox access was obtained.
register.action: Confirm whether financing is in go-live scope. If not, close. If yes, assign an owner.

register.summary: Uvation Rewards Platform API required for service credit sync
register.context: Service credit sync depends on the Rewards Platform API, currently tracked as an open dependency.
mitigation: Implement idempotent async processing via Service Bus
Run an hourly reconciliation job to catch missed/duplicate syncs
Alert Backend team on reconciliation discrepancies
register.why: Depends on Rewards API. Same failure mode as MT-1099, which Marketplace has already mitigated.
register.action: Reuse the Marketplace sync and reconciliation pattern.

register.summary: Service credit sync failure from Marketplace or Rewards
register.context: Service credit sync from Marketplace or Rewards can fail, risking inconsistent balances for customers.
mitigation: Implement idempotent async processing via Service Bus
Run an hourly reconciliation job
Alert on discrepancies detected during reconciliation

register.summary: CDN infrastructure must be operational to serve product images
register.context: Product image delivery depends on CDN infrastructure being operational. This is owned by DevOps and currently open.
mitigation: Validate CDN uptime SLA
Implement fallback image hosting for CDN outages
Monitor CDN health as part of standard observability

register.summary: Rewards platform sync failure leading to incorrect point balances
register.context: Sync failures between Marketplace and the Rewards platform can leave customers with incorrect point balances.

Add a manual reconciliation process for detected discrepancies
Alert Backend team on repeated sync failures

register.summary: Data breach exposing customer PII or order history
register.context: Customer PII and order history are high-value targets; a breach would have critical impact and reputational/legal consequences.
mitigation: Enforce encryption at rest and in transit for all PII and order data
Enforce role-based access control (RBAC) across services touching this data
Maintain a SOC2 audit trail for access to sensitive data

register.summary: Uvation Identity must remain single source of truth for USP auth
register.context: USP must not implement standalone authentication; all auth flows must delegate to Azure AD B2C via OAuth 2.0.

All authentication delegated to Azure AD B2C via OAuth 2.0
Periodic audit confirms no auth bypass paths exist

register.summary: Azure AD B2C outage preventing USP portal login
register.context: An Azure AD B2C outage would block USP portal login entirely without mitigation in place.

Maintain cached session tokens so active sessions survive brief outages
Link a status page on the login error screen

register.summary: Cloud partner API rate limits blocking dashboard data
register.context: Cloud partner API rate limits can block real-time dashboard data from loading.
mitigation: Implement a caching layer with a 5-minute TTL

Alert Engineering team when sustained rate-limiting is detected

issues.title: Policy change identified during UAT is not recorded anywhere in Jira
issues.impact: Not measurable from Jira. The change is not logged, so its effect on scope, dates and effort cannot be traced.
issues.rootCause: No change-request ticket type, and no UAT sign-off step that captures business-policy changes. About 300 tickets mentioning policy or change requests across 8 projects were checked. The closest are the returns-policy use cases (MT-1116, MT-1180, MT-1181, MT-1187) and MT-1286, which made the return-eligibility window configurable on 2 Sep. None of them records a change found in UAT.
issues.preventive: Log it now as a Change Request with impact and effort, linked to the affected stories. Add a 'business rules confirmed' line to UAT sign-off covering returns, refunds, loyalty points and pricing. Open business-rule questions already exist on MT-978 (loyalty points) and MT-1488 (refund and exchange timelines).

issues.title: AI Factory final prices calculated wrongly in production
issues.impact: The subscription price API returns the wrong final price for every billing and term combination in the Traditional, Modular and Nuclear AI Factory. One logged example expected 174,420 and got 150,660, about 14% low. A separate S1 has the Document API failing with a 502 on the first request.
issues.rootCause: Not recorded yet. The Document API failure is suspected to be the API gateway blocking the first request (comment on USP-4231, 28 Sep).
issues.actionTaken: All three are S1 and still in To Do on 6 Oct. Their due date was moved from 30 Sep to 30 Oct on 2 Oct. No fix recorded.
issues.preventive: Add the price-calculation checks to the automated regression run before each production release.

utilisationNotes.attributionWarning: Tempo writes every worklog to Jira under its own app account, so Jira cannot say who logged an hour. Hours here are credited to each ticket's current assignee. When a developer's ticket is handed to QA, the developer's hours move with it. Any day above 10 hours for one person is flagged for this reason.
utilisationNotes.overheadGap: Meetings, stand-ups and leave are logged on 13 shared overhead tickets in Uvation Projects, which is outside this report's scope, so that time is not in these totals.

deepDives.finding: Logged 39.8 hours on 9 working days in the 22 Sep–5 Oct window (2 Oct had no logged work from anyone), on PC-133 and PC-136. That averages about 4.4 hours a day against an 8-hour day, or 55% of the 72-hour capacity. 28 Sep shows 0.5 hours.
deepDives.context: The 5.5 hours on 17 Sep covered Dell GPU corrections with Naman and then HPE validation, which is 3 products. Each product also needed a tech-spec table, long description, short description and product-card copy in HTML. Between 15 and 24 Sep Suganya validated 19 products for 4 brands and started the 8 Vera Rubin products, about 1.5 hours per product. PC-133 closed on 30 Sep.
deepDives.question: Where are the other 3 or so hours a day? They may be on overhead tickets, which Jira hides, or unlogged.
deepDives.verify: Pull Suganya's Tempo timesheet for 22 Sep–5 Oct and compare the total with 72 hours. The full catalogue re-check (PC-136), started 29 Sep and due 30 Sep, was still In Progress on 6 Oct.

deepDives.finding: Jira credits Sapavat with 86.5 hours in the 22 Sep–5 Oct window, 120% of the 72-hour capacity, with three days between 11.8 and 18 hours (23, 25 and 28 Sep). That is not plausible for one person: Marketplace tickets closed on 1 Oct are assigned to Sapavat and carry developer hours.
deepDives.context: Sapavat's own QA tasks show 0.5 to 2 hours each. For example, the navigation, homepage-module and facet UI updates for the category disable took 1 hour each (MT-1455 to MT-1457). Functional test on staging took 1.5 hours and the toggle test 1.5 hours (MT-1471, MT-1473).
